subject.title: fix(agents): distinguish z.ai code 1305 content rejection from generic overload

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate z.ai Coding Plan's signature-triggered rejection in the request/setup path, or retain standard 1305 rate-limit handling and document the provider incompatibility?
rationale: The returned payload is indistinguishable from z.ai's documented ordinary rate-limit response, so this shared formatter cannot safely infer content rejection; selecting a provider-specific prompt/preflight mitigation versus diagnostic-only handling requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Add provider-aware mitigation
options.body: Handle the z.ai Coding Plan route where endpoint and request context are available, avoiding or preflighting the rejected signature while preserving normal prompts elsewhere.

options.title: Retain rate-limit semantics
options.body: Keep code 1305 classified according to the provider contract and document the incompatibility until z.ai supplies a distinct signal or changes behavior.

options.title: Accept ambiguous guidance
options.body: Merge probabilistic content-filter copy for every matching 1305 response and explicitly own the false-positive user guidance.

recommendation.title: Add provider-aware mitigation
recommendation.body: Handle the z.ai Coding Plan route where endpoint and request context are available, avoiding or preflighting the rejected signature while preserving normal prompts elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the z.ai provider boundary, onboarding, and the current error-copy area, making this the best available routing candidate.
